package_info.package_versions: N/A (applies to any version with unprotected batching)
package_info.why_malicious: The API implementation allows unlimited query batching, enabling attackers to bypass rate limiting and perform brute-force attacks or mass data enumeration, leading to credential compromise and denial of service.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends multiple user profile queries in a single HTTP request, bypassing per-request rate limits, resulting in mass user enumeration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Batching multiple queries in a single request to enumerate user objects is a classic enumeration technique and can be used to exfiltrate large amounts of data quickly.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects rate limiting to restrict the number of user objects retrievable per time window; batching circumvents this.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Fetching multiple dashboard widgets or related objects in a single request for performance.
key_indicators: Unusually large number of queries in a single request

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends 100 login mutation attempts for the same username but different passwords in a single HTTP request, bypassing rate limiting and enabling credential brute-forcing.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Sending a large number of authentication attempts in a single request is a brute-force attack pattern, especially when rate limiting is expected to prevent such behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal authentication expects one login attempt per request, with rate limiting enforced per attempt; batching allows mass attempts in one request.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; legitimate clients should never attempt multiple logins for the same user in a single request.
key_indicators: Multiple login mutations for the same user in a single request
High volume of authentication attempts in one payload

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a single GraphQL request containing a large batch of queries or mutations (e.g., multiple user enumerations or login attempts).
attack_chain.leads_to: Server processes all batched operations without enforcing per-operation rate limits.

attack_chain.action: Server returns all results in a single response, allowing attacker to enumerate users or brute-force credentials rapidly.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker obtains sensitive data (user profiles, valid session tokens) or causes denial of service.

behavioral_signatures: Single GraphQL request containing an unusually high number of operations (queries or mutations)
Multiple authentication attempts for the same user in a single request
Sequential object enumeration patterns in batched queries
file_indicators: No specific file indicators; detection is based on API payload structure and volume
network_indicators: POST /graphql requests with large JSON arrays in the body
High-frequency requests with large payloads to GraphQL endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor GraphQL endpoint traffic for requests containing large batches of operations, especially those targeting sensitive mutations (e.g., login) or sequentially enumerating object IDs. Flag requests with more than a reasonable number of batched operations (e.g., >5) or with repeated mutations for the same user. Implement server-side logic to enforce per-operation rate limits and limit the number of batched operations per request.
